terra.problem: Being seized does not establish whether carrying the cross was Simon's idea.
The claim that Jesus does not say why He tells them to weep overlooks His warning about the coming days in verses 29–31.
The passage does not establish that the women from Galilee were absent from the earlier group of women.
Jesus does say more about the coming days in verses 30–31, so the claim that He does not spell out more is inaccurate.
“Same words” claims an exact match, but the explanation has not identified matching words.
The passage does not say the disciples are absent from the scene.
Luke calls the two men criminals but does not explicitly say they are not disciples. It also does not say they are walking beside Jesus.
“Right beside Him” specifies a proximity the passage does not give. It says one was on His right and the other on His left.
“Right next to Him” specifies a proximity the passage does not give.
The passage does not specify that the people Jesus asks forgiveness for are the people around Him.
The claim that this happens in Jerusalem draws on context outside the supplied passage and needs a reference.
“Right as the sun is darkened” asserts precise simultaneity that the passage does not specify.
The passage does not establish that nobody else around the centurion says what he says about Jesus.
The passage does not say nobody is cheering or that the walk home is quiet.
The passage says the people return home beating their breasts, but it does not say there is no cheering at all.
